title: Nick's club in Greenwich Village
summary: Leeman describes Nick's on 10th Street and 7th Avenue, its two pianos, Hank Duncan and Sidney Bechet.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Nick's was on 10th Street and 7th Avenue.

And was always known as Dixieland or Nixiland, they used to call it -- Nick Rongetti used to be at the bar there during the war years, and he was a piano player, he always had two pianos going. Hank Duncan worked there also, a great pianist -- he used to play double piano, and nobody knows this, but he used to go out on the road when Fats Waller had two pianos. Nobody knows. That's why Hank adopted a lot of Fats Waller songs. He was the solo pianist there.
And for awhile, they brought in --
Sidney Becket was with him, and played with Zutty.
